summary:
Qwen3.5-9B: 36 parts passed the screen, all of them MLP clusters of 20 to 2048 units. They cover six skills: capital cities, facts, past tense, ordinal words, weekday successor and colour naming. Three parts failed the held-out check and two failed against random same-size parts (both at 2048+ units). No whole blocks or attention-head groups passed.

**How the clusters were built.** Attribution scans return at most 20 units, so the larger clusters were grown from the weights:
1. Take 3–14 attribution seeds in one layer.
2. Score every unit in that layer by how much its down column and gate/up rows project onto the seeds' span.
3. Subtract the same score for the other skills' seed sets, weighted 1× or 1.5×, and take the top K.

The 1.5× weighting was what stopped the leaks at large K: ordinal clusters leaking into weekday, and capital clusters leaking into facts.

**Passed (drop on the target skill):**
| Skill | Layer | Units → drop |
|---|---|---|
| capital_city | L31 | 20 → .528, 64 → .588, 256 → .334, 512 → .291, 1024 → .276, 2048 → .332 (random parts ≤ .052) |
| facts | L31 | 20 → .403, 128 → .274, 256 → .321, 512 → .280, 1024 → .222 |
| facts | L2 | 128 → .19 (looks like an early stage that builds entity tokens) |
| past_tense | L20 | 128 → .232, 256 → .251, 512 → .237, 1024 → .237, 2048 → .241 |
| ordinal_words | L31 | 64 → .439, 128 → .443, 256 → .390, 512 → .390, 1024 → .400 |
| weekday_successor | L30 | 128 → .224, 256 → .218, 512 → .197, 1024 → .224 (month barely moves) |
| weekday_successor | L27 | 256 → .180, 1024 → .175 |
| weekday_successor | L22 | 256 → .165 |
| color_naming | L26 | 256 → .187, 1024 → .177, 2048 → .187 |

**Size limit.** At 2048–4096 units, random parts of the same size start to match the weekday and colour clusters, and those parts failed the random-part check. Of the clusters that passed, the 2048-unit colour and past-tense ones are weak evidence for the same reason. Capital is the exception: it still clearly beats random parts at 2048 units.

**Negative findings:**
- Clusters picked only by how strongly units write a skill's tokens (logit lens) did not change the skill when removed.
- Removing whole blocks, whole MLPs or whole attention sublayers hit many skills at once. The full L31 attention sublayer is broad as well.
- Attention-head groups were not selective. The best tries (L23 for facts, L18 for ordinal, the L17 and L30 calendar heads) either stayed near .15 or moved control scores too.
- Mid-layer clusters (L12–L21) plateaued at .10–.148.
- Roman numerals reached about .11 and month about .13; code reached .10 at L31.
- No cluster was found for multilingual, math or plural nouns.
- Weekday and month share circuitry at L12–L20; only seeds from L22, L27 and L30 separate them.
- I could not define new skills because the agent skill cap was already reached.

summary:
Qwen3.5-9B session: nothing new was catalogued. All 7 screens failed; I also ran about 34 ablations and 9 attribution scans, within the 0.6 h limit.

**Screens (all failed):**
1. **L26 MLP, 128 units, roman numerals.** Grown from unit 4058, whose down_proj writes XX/XXX/XI/XII. Clean but too weak: roman dropped .127 (bar is .15), other skills ≤.019, random parts ≤.001, held-out also failed.
2. **L23 heads [0,5,9,12], ordinal.** Ordinal dropped .467, but the matched control moved .217 and random head sets reached .446.
3. **L27 heads [1,12,13,15], ordinal.** Ordinal dropped .091, which random head sets matched.
4. **L30 heads, 8 (pairs 8-9, 12-15, 26-27), colour.** Colour dropped .209 but leaked into calendar and ordinal skills.
5. **L30 heads [8,9,12,13], colour.** Colour dropped .157 and beat random, but leaked weekday .11, month .12 and ordinal .17.
6. **L30 heads [0,1,28,29], past tense.** Past tense dropped .084; month dropped .23.
7. **L25 heads [0,1,10,11], capital city.** Capital dropped .074, no better than random.

**Main structural finding:** weekday and month share one sequence circuit, often with ordinal attached. It shows up in:
- L19 full-attention heads 8–15 (weekday .381 / month .341, most other skills under .07)
- L19 heads 12–15 (.261 / .154)
- L23 head group 0
- L30 linear-attention heads
- an L12 MLP cluster grown from units 1877/6590

Because they always move together, no single-skill part could pass a screen. Defining a merged calendar/sequence skill would let the L19 heads be catalogued as a large, selective unit.

**Roman support is split** between L26 unit 4058 and L28 unit 480 (writes VI/IV/IX).

**Recipes that did nothing here:**
- Unembedding-subspace ranking at L24–31.
- Plural clusters grown from singular↔plural units.
- Multilingual clusters grown at L12/L16.
- An L31 digit-writer cluster (math .007). Instead of hurting, it raised calendar and ordinal scores by .1–.28.
- Math and code attribution was near zero everywhere.

summary: Short run on Qwen3.5-9B (L28-31 MLP, unembedding-subspace scoring with a 1.5x penalty on other categories). Findings: (1) Month-subspace clusters (256 units) at L31 and L30 IMPROVED month_successor when ablated (-.278 / -.077) with controls flat, so they act as month suppressors or competitors, not month writers. The L28 version was inert. (2) The L31 plural-subspace 256 cluster was inert on plural_nouns (.024). (3) The L31 Roman-numeral-subspace 256 cluster did nothing for roman_numeral (.014) but cut ordinal_words .302 (control .064, weekday .067). Its screen failed because one random 256-unit L31 part dropped ordinal .35. L31 ordinal is diffuse enough that random parts sometimes hit it. 1 screen used, 0 passed.
